ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given that $O$ is a point on line $AB$, and $OC \perp OE$. As shown in Figure (1), if $\angle COA = 34^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $OC\perp OE$ and $\angle COA = 34^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BOE = 180^\circ-90^\circ-34^\circ = \boxed{56^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Given that $O$ is a point on line $AB$, and $OC \perp OE$. As shown in Figure (1), if $\angle COA = 34^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle BOE$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the attached figure there are three small diagrams, and the problem specifies Figure 1. In Figure 1, A, O, and B are on the same horizontal straight line, with O between A and B; from O a ray OC is drawn toward the upper left, and a ray OE is drawn toward the upper right; a right-angle mark is drawn between OC and OE, indicating OC ⟂ OE. Then reason: Because A, O, and B are collinear, from OA to OB forms a straight angle, which is 180°. According to the order above Figure 1, this straight angle is composed of ∠AOC, ∠COE, and ∠EOB. The problem gives ∠COA=∠AOC=34°, and OC ⟂ OE, so ∠COE=90°. Therefore 34°+90°+∠BOE=180°, solving gives ∠BOE=180°-90°-34°=56°.
